brief: ING's daily rates note flags that the UST 10yr yield has touched 5%, with a Fed rate decision pending. Logic suggests a 25bp hike should calm the long end, but ING argues the back end is volatile enough that a hike validating recent trading could instead become an excuse to break above 5% and keep rising. The real question is whether the move extends to 6%: drivers are productivity growth expectations (good), Treasury issuance pressure (bad), and the Iran war's effect on oil and inflation (ugly). ING does not see 5% itself as pivotal, calling it merely a 50bp premium over a neutral zone, though it does raise mortgage/funding costs and worsens debt dynamics given long-dated Treasury financing. A rise to 6% within a month would be damaging; a gradual six-month move would be less disruptive. ING is not forecasting 6%, just weighing it, and expects cooling 2027 inflation and a growing rate-cut discount to eventually cap the move. Markets are increasingly nervous: the VIX has risen off its lows and implied rate volatility has spiked to levels last seen in April.
